fatal_errors: The baseline incorrectly assigns greater than 50% ductility to HfMoTaTiZr; that value belongs to HfNbTaTiZr, whereas as-cast HfMoTaTiZr has roughly 11.6% room-temperature compressive fracture strain.
The proposed Hf-to-V substitution does not reconstruct the target intervention of adding 4.2 at.% Cr to form HfMoTaTiZrCr0.5.
The cited evidence supports only the broad use of lower-density elements in RHEAs and provides no direct evidence that replacing Hf with V will preserve HfMoTaTiZr strength or ductility.
The experiment compares tensile properties against values largely reported from compression, making its performance thresholds non-equivalent to the relevant baseline.
The falsification rule is logically too strict: failure of any tested composition would reject a hypothesis that only predicts an optimum somewhere in the tested range.
explanation: The proposal addresses density reduction and offers a testable compositional series, so it is a plausible alternative alloy-design idea. However, it misses the target Cr-addition intervention, the approximately 3.8–4 vol.% reticulated Cr2(Ti,Zr,Hf,Ta) Laves phase, and the dual mechanism of lattice-distortion hardening plus crack-path hindrance/plasticity compensation. It consequently does not predict the observed 1750.6 MPa yield strength, 14.0% fracture strain, or 535.8 HV0.3 hardness. Its most serious weakness is the conflated baseline: the greater-than-50% ductility of HfNbTaTiZr is attributed to HfMoTaTiZr. Although density, XRD, microscopy, and mechanical tests are proposed, quantitative strain rate, compression geometry, thermal exposure, replication, and phase-morphology criteria are absent. The generic cited RHEA literature cannot validate the claimed retention of approximately 855 MPa at 1000 °C after V substitution.
